page: Microsoft Azure D64nlds_v6 is a dedicated virtual machine instance within the Dnldv6 family, running on the x86_64 architecture with an Intel processor under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of memory, resulting in a compute-oriented allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This low-memory ratio targets workloads that demand significant core count and compute throughput without incurring the cost of standard memory densities.

Local storage comprises a 3,780 GB NVMe SSD volume, and the server supports Premium Storage attachments for persistent disk configurations. The hardware configuration features zero GPUs and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Network optimization is natively incorporated, balancing high-capacity processor throughput with low-latency local disk input and output.

Cost efficiency is achieved by right-sizing RAM allocation, preventing excess expenditure on unused memory for CPU-bound applications. The operational tradeoff is limited headroom for memory-intensive caching or in-memory analytics. Workloads aligned with this server profile include large-scale batch processing, software compilation and CI/CD pipelines, high-concurrency web serving, and disk-intensive data transformation jobs utilizing the local NVMe storage.
